kind: wrong-limit-and-wrong-examples (prose; the valid example does not compile)
claim: The page states the symbol-length limit as 32 and builds its examples on it. pnut-ts v1.55.8 rejects a 31-character name with 'Symbol exceeds 30 characters' (VAR + `LONG this_is_exactly_31_characters_x`; a 30-character name compiles: idcheck.py id8/id9). The 'valid, 32 chars' example `this_is_exactly_32_characters_x` (:67) is 31 characters and is rejected. The invalid example `this_identifier_is_way_too_long_33` (:82) is 34 characters, not 33. `the_current_motor_speed_value_now` (:155, '30 chars') is 33. The same KB says 30 in spin2-getting-started.yaml:478 and S-147 registers 30; the v55 text itself says 32 (spin2-v55-text.txt:166), so v55 and the compiler disagree and the page followed the document. The gated block #153 (the 34-char name) is a `never` whose compile error is real ('Symbol exceeds 30 characters') while the page's number is wrong.
mark: traced (compiler); the document-vs-compiler conflict itself is an upstream lead

claim: Four operator statements in the tutorial's essential_operators table are wrong. (1) :294 comparison operators `== <> < > =< =>`: Spin2 spells them `<=` and `>=`; `=<` is rejected (g10/t/c1.spin2: 'Expected end of line (m281)'); class of S-052, here in prose. (2) :300 `bitwise: "&& || ! (bitwise versions)"`: `&&` and `||` are the LOGICAL AND / OR (synonyms of AND, OR; the table :489, :491 'Logical AND/OR ... returns 0 or -1'); only `!` is a bitwise operator (bitwise NOT), and `&` `|` `^` are the bitwise AND/OR/XOR the same page lists in :304. (3) :299 lists NOT as the logical NOT but not its symbol `!!`. (4) :311 `post_effects: "~~ (post-set), !! (post-clear)"`: `var~` is post-clear and `var~~` post-set; `var!!` is post-logical-NOT (0 -> -1, non-0 -> 0); `!!` is not post-clear.

The DITTO iteration index is `$$` (v50), not `$`: the feature line reads '$ (double-dollar) - iteration index within DITTO blocks' and the example is `LONG $77777777 + $   ' $ is 0, 1, 2, 3`. In the source `$$` is the 0..count-1 index and `$` is the origin (use of `$` is for branching inside the block). The block compiles (gate: program, PASS), but it generates $77777777 plus the origin, not +0..+3, so the comment is false; with `$$` it compiles too (g10/t/c5.spin2). Related to S-119 / S-192, which have the symbols the other way round.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/spin2-v55/spin2-v55-text.txt:42 (v50 note: 'A special index variable $$ ... iterates from 0 to count - 1 ... To branch within the block, use $ (origin)')

claim: `serial.start(63, 62, 115_200)` and `serial.start(RX_PIN, TX_PIN, 115_200)` call jm_fullduplexserial's start with three arguments. The object is `pub start(rxpin, txpin, mode, baud) : result` (four parameters): the baud rate would land in `mode` and `baud` would be missing, so the call does not compile against the real object. The gate passes :397 because the harness stub `serial.start(3)` takes the three arguments the block uses; the stub cannot know the object's real signature. (The other objects in the tutorial check out: jm_pwm exists; the P2ES control / matrix methods used on the hardware pages exist with the arities used.)

kind: wrong-syntax (does not compile; block not in the gate's candidate set)
claim: `debugging_support.basic_example` is `DEBUG("Value: ", DEC value)`. DEBUG formatters take parentheses; `DEC value` is rejected inside a method with 'Expected an expression term (m172)' (g10/t/d1.spin2, pnut-ts -d). The correct form is `DEBUG("Value: ", DEC(value))`. The sibling in the PASM2 guide (`DEBUG("Counter: ", UDEC(count))`, pasm2-getting-started.yaml:553-554) compiles in a method and in a DAT (d2, d3). Neither is a gate candidate (see O6).

kind: tool-behaviour stated as KB fact; wrong command name and error texts
severity: drives wrong code (every command line fails when copied)
claim: The compiler is called `pnut_ts` throughout (underscore). The installed command is `pnut-ts` (hyphen; `which pnut_ts` finds nothing, `pnut-ts --help` shows the options); the page's terminal command is `pnut-term-ts` (hyphen) in the same file, so the page is also inconsistent with itself. The option list (-l -v -q -o -d -F -D -I) matches `pnut-ts --help` v1.55.8, which also has -m -a -i -O -U -C and others the page omits. `common_errors` quotes four messages as the compiler's: 'Expected unique symbol', 'Symbol is not defined', "Expected '#' or constant", 'Value exceeds $1FF'. pnut-ts v1.55.8 says 'Symbol is already defined (m540)' (duplicate label), 'Undefined symbol', and 'Constant must be from 0 to 511 (m130)' (a 512 immediate); no message with the other wording was found. `jmp done` (no #) compiles, so "Expected '#' or constant" is not what a missing # produces either. pnut-term-ts is not installed here: its options (-d -t -p -b -l, default 2000000 baud) are NOT CHECKED. Doctrine: tool behaviour is not a KB fact; these belong to the tool's own help, not a table of quoted messages.
source: pnut-ts --help; pnut-ts -q on g10/t/e1..e5.spin2 (m130, m540, 'Undefined symbol')

kind: formula typo and a figure that does not follow
claim: `burst_size.calculation` is '((MAX_CS_LOW_USEC * (freq/1000000)) - 132) >> 4) << 4': the parentheses do not balance (one opening parenthesis is missing at the front). The driver's line is `burst := (((MAX_CS_LOW_USEC*(freq/1000000)) - 132) >> 4) << 4`. `typical_at_200mhz: "approximately 1280 bytes per burst"` does not follow from it: at 200 MHz, 8*200 - 132 = 1468, >> 4 << 4 = 1456. The block-level API in code_patterns (:337-390) matches the driver (start, startx, read, write, fill*, ERR_* values).

`group: [LED_PIN, led_pin, Led_Pin, LedPin, ledpin]  meaning: All refer to the same constant`. Case is ignored; underscores are not. `LedPin` and `ledpin` are a different name from `LED_PIN` / `led_pin` / `Led_Pin`. Two groups (:43, :46) are right.
source: language rule (case-insensitive, underscore is a character); the identifier rules the same file cites

claim: `BUTTON = 32` then `if INA[BUTTON]` and the comment 'Read current state of button pin from INA register' (:39). INA holds P31..P0 (the KB's own register map: pasm2-getting-started.yaml:227-232 INA P31..P0, INB P63..P32), so P32 is INB[0]. `INA[32]` compiles (g10/t/c6.spin2) but names a bit beyond the 32-bit register; what it reads is not shown by a source. The block is already red under S-002 for `DIRL #BUTTON`; its fix should use PINREAD(BUTTON) or INB[0].
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/silicon-doc/silicon-doc-text.txt (INA/INB definition) and the pasm2 guide register table; semantics of INA[32] undetermined

claim: `REPEAT idx FROM 99 TO 0 STEP -1`. The tutorial itself says 'FROM/TO order determines direction' (:256) and the v55 form is 'stepping by +/-<delta>' (spin2-v55-text.txt:763-766), i.e. the direction comes from FROM/TO and the delta is a magnitude. A negative STEP in a downward loop is the S-099 question (direction override); it compiles but the runtime behaviour was not tested here (no silicon).

kind: unsourced rule and unsourced syntax in prose
claim: 'Local labels can shadow global labels within their scope' has no source (spin2-v55-text.txt documents local symbols only as 'regular and local symbols ... not accessible outside your in-line PASM code', :813); a `.name` local carries its global's prefix, so there is nothing to shadow.
